- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 10–15 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true values show a clear downward trend or mean reversion.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — e.g., after 80+ prices, model often predicts 70–75, but true drops to 60–65.
- Model tends to ignore recent downward momentum in the history, especially when the last 5–7 days show strong decline — forecasts remain “sticky” to prior highs.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — e.g., after a 1–2 day spike, model predicts a sustained high, but true price often corrects within 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates the impact of seasonal or calendar-driven downward pressure (e.g., end-of-month or winter dip patterns) — especially in the last 10 days of the forecast.
- Model shows “lag” in adjusting to new information — e.g., if true price drops sharply after day 10, model still holds high values for days 15–20.
